僕のヒーローアカデミア [Boku no Hero Academia] #28

My Hero Academia, Vol. 28

Kohei Horikoshi

4.59
7,128 ratings409 reviews
Rate this book
What would the world be like if 80 percent of the population manifested superpowers called “Quirks”? Heroes and villains would be battling it out everywhere! Being a hero would mean learning to use your power, but where would you go to study? The Hero Academy of course! But what would you do if you were one of the 20 percent who were born Quirkless?

The all-out war against the Paranormal Liberation Front continues at the hospital and the mountain villa! Mirko desperately battles High-Ends in order to reach Tomura’s stasis tank, knowing exactly how much is at stake if she fails. At the PLF hideout, Dabi is determined to roast Hawks, but Tokoyami isn’t about to let his mentor fall. Meanwhile, while helping to evacuate the city, Midoriya senses an ominous presence in the hospital… With things going from bad to worse, and the heroes’ forces battered and stretched thin, Midoriya realizes the time has come for him to join the fight, even if it may be his last.

About the author

Kohei Horikoshi

380 books2,663 followers
HORIKOSHI Kouhei
Name (in native language): 堀越耕平
Associated Names:
Kouhei Horikoshi

Born 1986 in the prefecture Aichi, Horikoshi first attracted attention in the second half of 2006 when he entered Shueisha's 72th Tezuka Award for Newcomers with his one shot "Nukegara" and made it to the final six, where he gained himself an "Honorable Mention".
Various short stories in Shueisha's Akamaru JUMP followed over the years until he published his one shot "Oumagadoki Doubutsuen" in issue #2/2010 of Weekly Shounen JUMP.

Kouhei Horikoshi is a graduate of Nagoya University of Arts. He was previously an assistant to TANAKA Yasuki.

The battle, Shigaraki’s insane new power levels, Deku’s terror yet determination to protect those he loves yet keep One For All away from Shigaraki…this series has taken a very insane, dark turn that doesn’t stop pulling any punches and flings plot twists left and right, and even though I’m in pain right alongside the characters it’s so good I both love it and can’t stop reading every time I pick up a volume.

My Hero Academia, Vol. 28 continues where the previous tankōbon left off and contains the next nine chapters (268–276) of the on-going manga series.

The all-out war against the Paranormal Liberation Front continues at the hospital and the mountain villa of Jaku City. Rumi Usagiyama as Mirko desperately battles High-Ends in order to reach Tomura Shigaraki’s stasis tank, knowing exactly how much is at stake if she fails. Unfortunately, fails she does as Tomura Shigaraki awakens more powerful than ever as he has inherited the All For One quirk.

Sensing the awakening, Izuku Midoriya who is a part of the evacuation team, warns everyone to leave the area as the hospital is utterly destroyed. Sensing One For All nearby, Tomura Shigaraki calls for him. Izuku Midoriya wastes no time and leads Tomura Shigaraki, who is fighting Enji Todoroki as Endeavor at the time, to a place where there is no people so they can fight. Katsuki Bakugō to fight by his side as he has a stake in the fight with All For One.

The tankōbon closes with Sorahiko Torino as Gran Torino taking Izuku Midoriya and Katsuki Bakugō out of the way, because they can’t afford to let Tomura Shigaraki have the All For One quirk at any and all costs. As the pair watches Shōta Aizawa as Eraserhead take on Tomura Shigaraki head-on.

Kohei Horikoshi has written and illustrated this tankōbon. It mainly focuses on the awakening of Tomura Shigaraki and the immense power he has received thanks to the efforts of Maruta Shiga who gave him the powers of All For One. Izuku Midoriya sensing his awakening heads to a relatively empty space to confront Tomura Shigaraki with his old friend Katsuki Bakugō following him. This tankōbon serves as a prelude to the ultimate confrontation between Izuku Midoriya and Tomura Shigaraki the inheritors of One For All and All For One quirks respectively.

All in all, My Hero Academia, Vol. 28 is a good continuation of the series that seems really intriguing and I can't wait to read what happens next.

Tch...! I just fuckin' got that... "Hosu City" is named after Hoth!

The worst part about owning these volumes physically is I can't read them at night in bed when trying to fall asleep. I mean, I could read them on MangaPlus, but then it's a waste of money to have bought the volumes. As a consequence, I'd gotten further in Black Clover, which I've been reading purely digitally. My plan was to eventually balance them out, with BnHA maintaining a lead because it started running first (iirc). Oh well, now they're tied!

This arc keeps building and building, and I guess we have our climax; Shigaraki has awakened, and he has All for One (the Quirk, not the dude) within him, on top of having his physical abilities boosted, and Decay having Awakened. There's word of Super Shigaraki being like a perfected Nomu, which reminds me of Wesker in Resident Evils CV and 5, which... works better here, as I'd rather have human Shigaraki than a bunch of samey Nomu (whereas in RE I strongly prefer having various mutated final bosses then just "Wesker with a single Ouroboros tentacle making a scythe out of airplane parts"...).
